messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: Set-up for IRACE package using a '.exe' file
parts:
Hi Rahul,

Please see the section  "Target runner executable program" in the user-guide. In a nutshell, you either need to make your .exe behave as the target-runner or  OR you need to write another program (script, .exe, BAT file) that behaves like the target-runner but internally calls your .exe. The target-runner accepts command-line arguments as specified in the user-guide and prints just one number and nothing else.

An example of the latter approach (a BAT script that calls an .exe) is below. Save it as target-runner.bat. You'll need to adjust the example to your needs and you have to make target-runner.bat executable and set "--target-runner target-runner.bat". Otherwise, it won't work.

Cheers,

Manuel.

::##############################################################################
:: BAT version of target-runner for Windows.
:: Contributed by Andre de Souza Andrade <andre....@uniriotec.br>.
:: Check other examples in examples/
::
:: This script is run in the execution directory (execDir, --exec-dir).
::
:: PARAMETERS:
:: %%1 is the candidate configuration number
:: %%2 is the instance ID
:: %%3 is the seed
:: %%4 is the instance name
:: The rest are parameters to the target-algorithm
::
:: RETURN VALUE:
:: This script should print one numerical value: the cost that must be minimized.
:: Exit with 0 if no error, with 1 in case of error
::##############################################################################
@echo off

:: Please change the EXE and FIXED_PARAMS to the correct ones
SET "exe=D:\bin\program"
SET "fixed_params=--time 20 --tries 1 --quiet"

FOR /f "tokens=1-4*" %%a IN ("%*") DO (
        SET candidate=%%a
        SET instance_id=%%b
        SET seed=%%c
        SET instance=%%d
        SET candidate_parameters=%%e
)

SET "stdout=c%candidate%-%instance_id%-%seed%.stdout"
SET "stderr=c%candidate%-%instance_id%-%seed%.stderr"

:: If the program just prints a number, we can use 'exec' to avoid
:: creating another process, but there can be no other commands after exec.
::
:: %exe %fixed_params% -i %instance% --seed %seed% %candidate_parameters%
:: exit 0
::
:: Otherwise, save the output to a file, and parse the result from it.

%exe% %fixed_params% -i %instance% --seed %seed% %candidate_parameters% 1>%stdout% 2>%stderr%

:: This is an example of reading a number from the output.
:: It assumes that the objective value is the first number in
:: the first column of the last line of the output.

setlocal EnableDelayedExpansion
set "cmd=findstr /R /N "^^" %stdout% | find /C ":""
for /f %%a in ('!cmd!') do set numberlines=%%a
set /a lastline=%numberlines%-1
for /f "tokens=3" %%F in ('more +%lastline% %stdout%') do set COST=%%F
echo %COST%

::del %stdout% %stderr%
exit 0

Dear Rahul,

Answers below:

On Tuesday, 12 June 2018 11:30:09 UTC+1, rahulroynit wrote:
Thank you Manuel for the information. Well, I am struggling at few places while trying to create the setup. 
1. I do not understand the scripting language, I mean how do I infer what does each line mean?

If you are not familiar with any scripting language, then it may be easier to just modify your code to accept input/output like target-runner would, and then just use your .exe file as the target-runner. Alternatively, you may also write the target-runner in C++ as a separate .exe file that calls your .exe file. I'll recommend to use --check to test that irace can communicate with your target-runner as expected.
2. Do I need to write my own set of coding lines in the target runner, or do I need to update the codes in the sample file only at few places?

It depends on what your target-runner needs to do. Every target-algorithm is different! Normally you need to customize: how you convert the parameter values that irace passes to target-runner to the parameter settings that your algorithm will use, how your target algorithm is called (path location, file setup) and how the output of your algorithm is parsed to extract the cost that irace cares about and print it.
3. How to create the instances in the instance.txt file? I do not have separate instance files.

Then you can set trainInstancesDir="" and in instances.txt, each line should be something that allows you to distinguish different instances. Example:

instance1
instance2
instance3

Then, irace will call target-runner with something like:

"target-runner 1 113 734718556 instance2 --eas --localsearch 0 --alpha 2.92 --beta 3.06 --rho 0.6 --ants 80"

It is the task of the target-runner to interpret what instance2 means and call your target-algorithm appropriately.  Irace does not require that instances are files (see the examples in the user-guide 5.4
 Training instances)

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.subject: Re: Set-up for IRACE package using a '.exe' file
parts:
Hi Rahul,

You don't need to do anything in R. If your .exe file is for example, "C:\folder\your.exe". Then just call irace with "irace.bat --target-runner "C:/folder/your.exe". Or create a file 'scenario.txt' that contains the line:

targetRunner = "C:/folder/your.exe"

then irace will try to call your.exe with the arguments described in the user-guide and it will expect that your.exe prints just a single number. Since your.exe is under your control, you should be able to change it to do just that (or create a new your.exe that does just that).

Try the following steps:

1. Create a file "scenario.txt" with the following content (update the path and file name of your.exe with your actual .exe file):

targetRunner="C:/folder/your.exe"
trainInstancesDir=""
trainInstancesFile="instances.txt"
maxExperiments=1000

2. Create a file "instances.txt" with the following content:

instance1
instance2

3. Create a file "parameters.txt" with the following content:

param1 "--param1 " i (1,10)

4. Open the shell in the same folder where all the above files are and run:

C:\path_to_irace_installed_files\bin\irace.bat --check

Or if you prefer to run irace from within R, then execute within R the following:

library(irace)
irace.cmdline("--check")

5. The above will fail with an error such as:

# Error occurred while executing targetRunner:
== irace == running command 'C:/bin/your.exe' testConfig1 instance1 1234567 instance1   --param1 5' had status 1

The reason is that your.exe needs to handle the arguments 'testConfig1 instance1 1234567 instance1   --param1 5' as described in the user-guide. If you get any other error, then either the paths to the various files are wrong, or your current directory does not contain the files, or your.exe needs to have executable permission, etc. Check what irace prints, it normally tells you very clearly why it did not work.

I hope the above helps.

Cheers,

Manuel.

parts:
Dear Rahul,

I'm surprised irace still works. If I try to do the same, I get:

Error: == irace == Both instancesDir and instancesFile are empty: No instances provided

In any case, it doesn't matter that it doesn't give you an error. You still need to tell irace which instances (benchmark, function, or whatever is an instance for your context) are used for training, so that irace can tell your algorithm what experiments it should perform. Otherwise, irace will believe that your algorithm is doing what irace told your algorithm to do, when actually your algorithm is completely ignoring what irace said and doing something different.

Moreover, I didn't understand this explanation that you mentioned: " Your example C++ code does not read anything from the command-line that irace is passing to it. You need to use argc and argv to do so." I didn't do anything in this regard, but still irace returned results.

Yes, your algorithm will run with the parameter values that it uses internally and it will return a value, but it is not using the parameter values that irace passed in the command-line.  Thus, irace cannot tune your algorithm because your algorithm ignores the values that irace is telling your algorithm to use. You need to read those values from the command-line and force your algorithm to use them. To make sure that your algorithm is using the parameter values passed by irace, set the default values to something invalid and, before using the parameter value, check that the value is valid. You may also print the values (and the instance) that your algorithm is using to some file and check that what irace told your algorithm to use matches with what your algorithm is actually using.
One last question, what does the mean value in the results column imply? I read its the mean of the configuration,but it didn't make any sense.

This is explained in the user guide (Section Output and results):

Mean best: Mean of the best configuration across the instances seen so far in this race.

Is the above not clear? If so, could you explain what is not clear so that we can improve the user guide?

Cheers,

Manuel.

parts:
On Tuesday, 19 June 2018 18:32:28 UTC+1, Rahul Roy wrote:
Thank you Manuel for such valuable information. 
When it says mean of the best configuration, what does mean of best configuration mean? I mean what does, say a value 10, represent in that column?

It means that at the current iteration (race), there is a set of configurations (variants of your algorithm with different parameter settings) evaluated on a number of instances (or pairs instance-seed if the number of instances is too low) . Each configuration when evaluated on each instance returns a cost value to irace. The mean cost value is computed over all instances seen so far. The mean value of the best configuration is the mean of the configuration that irace considers to be the best up to that point of the race (column Best). Which configuration is the best depends on the testType. For testType="t-test", it is the configuration with the lowest mean. For testType="F-test", it is the configuration with the lowest sum of ranks. The details are in the user-guide.

If you have 10, this means that the mean value returned by the best configuration over the instances seen so far in the current race is 10. Ideally the value should decrease over time, however, when the race sees another instance, this value may increase or decrease. If the best (Best column) changes, then the mean may change completely because it depends on the values returned by all configurations in all instances. But if your algorithm always returns a positive cost and you get a mean of -10 (or if your algorithm returns cost values between [0,1] and you get a mean of 10), then something is wrong somewhere (likely, in your target-runner).


Cheers,

Manuel.

If the best (Best column) changes, then the mean may change completely because it depends on the values returned by all configurations in all instances. But if your algorithm always returns a positive cost and you get a mean of -10 (or if your algorithm returns cost values between [0,1] and you get a mean of 10), then something is wrong somewhere (likely, in your target-runner).

On Sunday, 22 July 2018 07:00:53 UTC-4, Rahul Roy wrote:
Thank you Leslie!

I'm surprised that this happened because I didn't make any changes and all the irace runs were executed successfully. But all of a sudden, twice this message has come and irace stopped therein. Should I include them in the forbidden configurations file? Can you kindly help me with the way the forbidden configurations should be written in the file as I couldn't get much help from the user guide? The parameters are specified in the snapshot attached in the previous mail.

Well, if you know that this warning means that the algorithm is not working properly then you should include this 
configuration in the forbidden configurations file so irace will not try to test it. Before creating the file I would advice 
you to try to understand which is the parameter value or the combination of parameter values that are causing this problem. 
Once you know this you can create the file, lets assume that the problem is caused by the combination of the following parameters:

--METH1 ELLIPSOIDAL --PARA1 14.4541

so then the line in the forbidden configuration file should be:

(METH1 == "ELLIPSOIDAL") & (PARA1 == 14.4541)

Note that you should not use the flag of the parameter but the name, so this example assumes that the definition of the parameters is like this:

METH1   "--METH1 "  c  ("ELLIPSOIDAL", "OTHER")
PARA1   "--PARA1 "  r (0,20)

An alternative choice to the use of forbidden configurations would be to modify your target runner / executable to return Inf 
(again, the warning should NOT be printed). This will make irace to reject the configuration that generated this Inf result. 
This option is adviced when you dont know when the problem with your target algorithm happens. Check section 10.8 of the user guide for more details.

I hope this was useful.
Bests, 
Leslie.

Thanks and Regards,
Rahul
